newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks tops 1,000 stores in FY96.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks tops 1,000 stores in FY96.

text.p: Starbucks Corp executives said the company had exceeded 1,000 stores at the end of its fiscal year to September 27 and that revenues will top $690 million for the year, as analysts have forecast.

Speaking at a Montgomery Securities investment conference here, Starbucks Chief Financial Officer Michael Casey said the price of current green coffee, which had pressured margins earlier in the year, has fallen below price levels on its inventory.
He also told investors the company has strong cash flow from operations, partly to an effort to reduce inventory by more than $50 million.
Starbucks ended fiscal 1995 a year ago with 676 stores.
As a result, he said, without unexpected changes in its business environment or conditions, the company does not expect to require additional financing during fiscal 1997.

He declined comment on the results for the final quarter of Starbucks's fiscal year, which ended last Saturday, saying the Seattle-based retailer and wholesaler of gourmet coffee plans to release its full-year results on November 14.

Casey said the company expects on Thursday to announce its final fiscal year-end store tally, but that it should be at 1,004 or 1,005. This is up to 30 stores ahead of some Wall Street analyst projections.
The company opened 73 stores in its third quarter alone, bringing the total number to 899, and has expanded by more than 100 since then.
For the 39 weeks to June 30, 1996, Starbucks reported net earnings per share of $0.38 on net sales of $500.1 million, up from $0.29 a share on sales of $335.8 million a year earlier.

Starbucks President Orin Smith said the company added at least 324 stores in fiscal 1996 and was mulling the prospect of partnerships in Europe and Central and South America during its next fiscal year.
He said the mail order business has been growing by 25 percent and international was a key new area of attention, with two partnerships launched in Japan.
Smith said its business of ice cream products marketed with Dryers will produce profits in fiscal 1997.
